scope: Shared Timer/TimerTask scheduling on an actual dedicated platform worker per timer. No application/package/library name checks. SDK proof uses ordinary Java/Android APIs.

basis.implementation: Independent Rust adaptation of public Timer API contracts; no JDK Timer source code copied.

implementation.reentry: Queue borrows are dropped before task invocation. Callback ownership uses actual NativeHost.current_thread_id, with a single-interpreter identity only when no NativeHost is bound. Main-thread entry while a native worker releases VmGate is not labelled as a worker.
implementation.scheduling: One-shot, fixed-delay from actual start, and fixed-rate from previous planned due. Repeated work is serial; period/delay validation precedes queue mutation. Date overloads explicitly unavailable before mutation.
implementation.execution: All four constructors require successful BackgroundWorkers.start. No worker delivery occurs from the main Looper. VM callers serialize scheduling and callback entry with the platform VM lease.
implementation.state: Unique increasing per-runtime tokens, weak Timer owner, real queued/running task GC roots. Task cancellation retains queued references until purge/due/Timer.cancel. Uncaught task error terminates that timer and retains its exact error for Android pump.
implementation.bounds: 64 worker records plus pending error records,4096 attached task records,4096 queued entries across timers,4096-byte requested names. Backend may impose a lower real thread limit. Repeated i64 due overflow fails explicitly with TIMER_TIME_OVERFLOW.
implementation.metadata: Requested name and daemon flag retained per token. This does not implement OS thread names, Java Thread identity APIs or JVM daemon-driven process-exit policy.
implementation.clock: System.currentTimeMillis uses actual Clock.wall_time_millis. SystemClock/nanoTime retain elapsed-time behavior. Missing/failing clock and worker operations preserve exact errors; failed start/wake/cancel do not claim success.

host_coverage: Worker-required constructors, start failure, name null validation, retained constructor metadata, unique tokens.
Wall-time backward jump and separation from elapsed clock; main drawing never delivers TimerTask.
One-shot cancel return values and duplicate rejection; fixed-delay drift and fixed-rate catch-up.
Queued/running GC roots while Timer owner is collected; cancelled queue roots released by purge; token reuse prohibited.
Reentrant task scheduling and Timer.cancel; exact uncaught ArithmeticException survives worker step and next Android pump.
Backend start/wake/cancel and clock failure do not partially schedule or report fake success.
Nested native callback changes actual thread identity; worker Handler/Looper restrictions do not affect main.
SDK proof writes actual shared VFS file and posts a main Handler callback.

proof.expected: Three task lines with scheduled/actual epoch millis and noLooper=true; TIMER_PROOF_PASS elapsed=<measured milliseconds>. Actual TimerTask cancels its Timer and posts visible UI result via previously-created main Handler.

limits: Dedicated Horizon thread creation, real wait/wake latency, JNI attach/TLS detach, VM gate concurrency and actual NRO proof require separate transport tests and parent-run E2E.
Date scheduling overloads, OS-thread naming, Java Thread APIs and JVM daemon process-exit behavior are not verified/implemented by this Timer contract.
The host JVM oracle is Microsoft OpenJDK21, not an Android API26 reference device.
No Candy Crush or Mekorama runnable/gameplay claim follows from these host tests.
